subject: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medpivot.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As we prepare the Private (VPC) package for MedPivot I wanted to get alignment on three items you flagged: customer-managed keys, operator access boundaries, and the DPA addendum language for cross-border telemetry.

High-level ask: can you confirm the internal procurement/legal preferences below so we can produce a short addendum instead of a full DPA rewrite?

- KMS model: MedPivot prefers a customer-controlled KMS where keys are created and owned by you (customer) and Redwood has no export rights. Is that correct?
- Escrow/escrow-trigger: Do you need an escrow arrangement for recovery capability (e.g., M-of-N escrow with a neutral custodian) or is a documented breakglass procedure + encrypted backup acceptable?
- Operator entitlements: we propose a minimal operator role (breakglass only) with time-limited access, multi-approver jump box, and full audit trail. Would procurement require additional wording (e.g., prohibition on key re-export, criminal-subpoena handling, or external transfer restrictions)?

If you can confirm preferences we will: (a) draft a DPA addendum with explicit key ownership language and operator entitlements matrix, (b) propose SLA for access drills/audit evidence, and (c) share the operator-entitlements spreadsheet for your review.

Proposed next steps: quick 30-min sync next week to sign off on the addendum draft. Times I have open: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medpivot.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medpivot.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 13:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC

Ben —

Appreciate the follow-up. Confirming MedPivot's preferences at a high level:

- KMS: We require customer-held keys. Keys must be generated in our HSM (cloud vendor or on-prem HSM) and Redwood must not have the ability to export raw key material.
- Escrow: We prefer an escrow option. Our legal team will accept an M-of-N escrow with a neutral custodian OR a documented, audited breakglass procedure that provides equivalent recovery assurance. We will share the escrow PKI requirements if we go that route.
- Operator access: Acceptable only under strict breakglass conditions. Access must require a two-person approval workflow, be time-boxed, and include live session recording plus immutable audit logs.

Procurement/legal asks: please provide a draft addendum (redlines preferred) and any sample wording around judicial requests/subpoenas for key disclosure — we need to see how Redwood will handle lawful access requests for customer-controlled keys. Also include the SOC2 controls that apply to operator authentication + session recording.

Attaching: DPA_Addendum_v0.3.pdf (current template) — see section 4.2 for cross-border telemetry.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Legal Operations
MedPivot Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC

Looping you in — Elena confirmed customer-key requirement and wants either M-of-N escrow or an audited breakglass. Procurement wants sample wording for lawful access/judicial requests + SOC2 evidence for operator session controls.

Quick notes for the doc owners:
- Marissa: can we draft the key-ownership clause that states: "Customer retains sole ownership of KMS keys; Redwood will not possess or export key material. Operator access limited to ephemeral agent that never discloses key material." Keep it short and prescriptive.
- Vivek: need the ops controls paragraph: two-person approval, time-limited session, live session recording, immutable audit logs, and the SLA for providing logs within X days. Also note whether we can support M-of-N escrow (protocol and recommended custodians).
- Kimberly: procure/legal will require bullet language on subpoenas/judicial process and export restrictions; can you check standard language we have used in prior private deployments (see past threads) and propose two options (strict no-export vs. limited exceptions for court orders with notice and challenge window).

I'll propose a 30-min sign-off call Tue 10am PT. If you can't make that, propose alternatives. I'll draft the initial addendum and the entitlements matrix and place in Drive.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC

Ben / team —

I drafted a short key clause and an operator entitlements matrix (attached). High-level:

- Key custody: we will support customer-held keys via a KMS integration pattern (external KMS connector). Redwood will hold only a pointer/metadata record to the key; no private key bytes will be stored in Redwood systems. Clause: "Customer retains exclusive control of cryptographic key material. Redwood's runtime may reference keys via approved KMS connectors only and shall not persist, export, or have access to raw key material."

- Escrow: we can support an M-of-N escrow plan; recommend neutral custodians (e.g., Entrust or Keyfactor) and an offline PKI exchange model. If MedPivot prefers breakglass instead, we will provide documented playbooks + quarterly drills and signed audit reports.

- Operator entitlements: attached matrix is conservative: breakglass flow requires two approvers (one from customer, one from Redwood), ephemeral jump-host via customer-vpc with session recording forwarded to the customer's S3/GCS, and a max 4-hour session. All sessions immutable-logged and available for dispute resolution.

I've uploaded operator-entitlements-matrix.xlsx to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-op-entitlements

I'll work with Kimberly on two wording variants for subpoenas/judicial process. Vivek, can you confirm feasibility of streaming session recordings directly to customer storage?

Marissa

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medpivot.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medpivot.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 09:18:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Tenant secrets ownership & operator entitlements for private VPC

Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for the matrix, Marissa. A few clarifications from legal/procurement:

> From Marissa's matrix: "session recording forwarded to the customer's S3/GCS" — procurement asks that recordings be writen to MedPivot's retention bucket (not a Redwood bucket) and that the retention TTL be set by MedPivot. That aligns with our data governance.

Two small wording asks on the addendum draft:
1) Add explicit "no-export" phrase: "Redwood shall not export, copy, or transfer customer key material outside of the customer's controlled environment except as explicitly required by a lawful order and subject to the notice/challenge process."
2) Add a subsection about access drills: Redwood will provide drill evidence (signed statements + logs) within 5 business days of a request, quarterly.

Procurement has asked that we include SOC2 control IDs that map to operator authentication and session logging. If you can provide those controls (or SOC2 report excerpt) that would speed review.

If acceptable, procurement will route the short addendum for signature next week once the two wording items are in place.

— Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
